name: 2-channel 5 V relay module (high/low trigger)
description: Two Songle SRD-05VDC-SL-C 5 V relays (SPDT, form C) on one board, each driven by an optocoupler and transistor with a flyback diode: a GPIO switches two separate loads such as lamps, pumps or fans. Contacts rated 10 A 125 VAC / 7 A 240 VAC / 7 A 28 VDC (form C, resistive). Module supply 5 V; each energised coil draws about 71 mA. Modelled with both trigger jumpers set to H (high level trigger: IN high = relay on). Sold as: 2-channel 5V relay module with optocoupler, high and low level trigger selectable by jumper (input header DC+, DC-, IN1, IN2; outputs NO/COM/NC screw terminals per channel).
eli5: Two electrically controlled switches: when your board sets IN1 or IN2 high, a little click connects that channel's lamp, pump or fan to its own power.

pins.name: DC+
pins.description: Module supply, 5 V (powers the optocouplers and both relay coils, about 71 mA per energised relay); use the board's 5V/VBUS pin, not 3V3

pins.name: IN1
pins.description: Relay 1 control input. With its jumper on H: high = relay 1 on (NO1 connected to COM1), low = off. Optocoupler input, a few mA; 3.3 V or 5 V logic.

pins.name: IN2
pins.description: Relay 2 control input. With its jumper on H: high = relay 2 on (NO2 connected to COM2), low = off. Optocoupler input, a few mA; 3.3 V or 5 V logic.

supplierQuery: 2 channel 5V relay module optocoupler high low level trigger
buildNotes: Move BOTH trigger jumpers to H (high level trigger) before use: many boards ship set to L. On L the logic is inverted (IN low = relay on) and a 3.3 V GPIO may not switch the relay fully off.

Power DC+ from 5 V, not 3.3 V: the SRD-05VDC coil needs at least 3.75 V to pull in and draws about 71 mA per relay, which is too much for a GPIO or the 3V3 regulator. Share DC- with the microcontroller's GND.
Contacts (form C): 10 A 125 VAC, 7 A 240 VAC, 7 A 28 VDC resistive; inductive loads (motors, pumps) 3 A. Use the NO terminal for a load that should be off by default.
The relays switch in up to 10 ms and release in up to 5 ms, and the datasheet allows only about 30 operations per minute under load: never PWM a relay.

Mains wiring on the screw terminals is dangerous: keep it in a closed insulated box, never touch the board while it is plugged in, and leave mains to an adult/qualified person. For a first project switch a low-voltage DC load (a 12 V lamp or a 5 V pump).
Set the GPIO low at start-up (Pin(..., Pin.OUT, value=0)) so the relays do not click on while the board boots.

example.code:
from machine import Pin
import time

# Trigger jumpers on H: IN high = relay on.
relay1 = Pin({IN1}, Pin.OUT, value=0)
relay2 = Pin({IN2}, Pin.OUT, value=0)
while True:
    relay1.value(1)
    relay2.value(0)
    print('relay 1 ON, relay 2 OFF')
    time.sleep(2)
    relay1.value(0)
    relay2.value(1)
    print('relay 1 OFF, relay 2 ON')
    time.sleep(2)

test.title: Relay 1 and relay 2 take turns switching on

library.note: Passed the Sparkbench part check in simulation and matched an independent datasheet reading (2 difference(s) settled by a third reading with quoted evidence). Not yet tested on real hardware.
